method: Screen luminance is the light a screen sends back to the audience. The calculator splits the image diagonal into width and height for the chosen aspect ratio, because h = d / sqrt(a^2 + 1) for a = width / height, multiplies the two to get the screen area, and spreads the projector's light output over it. Illuminance on the screen is lumens divided by the area in square metres; screen luminance in foot-lamberts is lumens x screen gain / area in square feet, and in cd/m2 it is that figure x 3.4263, which is the same as lumens x gain / (pi x area in m2). Gain 1.0 is a plain matte white surface that reflects light evenly in every direction; a gain 2.4 screen returns 2.4 times the luminance at its centre but narrows the viewing cone. One foot-lambert is 1/pi candela per square foot and one foot is exactly 0.3048 m. Three targets are offered: the DCI cinema 2D value of 48 cd/m2 (14 fL) from SMPTE ST 431-1, the 16 fL (55 cd/m2) that 35 mm film prints were graded for under SMPTE 196M, and the 7 fL (24 cd/m2) of legacy lamp-based 3D projection. Working back, the lumens a target needs are target fL x area in ft2 / gain, and the largest screen that still reaches the target at the available light follows from the same equation. The result is a centre-of-screen figure: real screens fall off towards the edges, and lens transmission, port glass and lamp ageing all remove light, so treat the number as a best case. Inputs are limited to 10-1,000 in, 10-100,000 lm and gain 0.1-10. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: SMPTE ST 431-1:2006, D-Cinema Quality - Screen Luminance Level, Chromaticity and Uniformity: 48 cd/m2 (14 fL) at screen centre, with the side and corner uniformity limits.
DCI Digital Cinema System Specification and SMPTE RP 431-2, Reference Projector and Environment: the 48 cd/m2 reference white and its +/-10.2 cd/m2 theatre tolerance.
SMPTE 196M, Motion-Picture Film - Indoor Theater and Review Room Projection: 16 fL open gate (+/-1 fL review rooms) for 35 mm film presentation.
DCI High Frame Rate Digital Cinema Recommended Practice (2015): legacy 3D peak white 24 cd/m2 +/- 6.9 (7 fL) through the glasses, and 48 cd/m2 for laser-illuminated 3D.
NIST SP 811, Guide for the Use of the International System of Units: the foot as exactly 0.3048 m and the foot-lambert as 1/pi candela per square foot.
